newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania plans to ban or penalise sugar imports.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania plans to ban or penalise sugar imports.

text.p: Lithuania plans to impose a temporary ban on sugar imports or a punishing 100 percent import duty to protect local producers, the agriculture ministry said on Thursday.

"One of the immediate problems to be solved (in 1997) is the temporary banning of sugar and raw sugar imports to Lithuania or the increasing the import duty for sugar to 100 percent," the ministry said in a statement.
"Current customs duty of 35 percent does not defend the Lithuanian market," the agriculture ministry spokeswoman Regina Ramutyte told Reuters.
The proposal is expected to be considered during a cabinet meeting next week.
As above-the-quota sugar prices have fallen on the world market, cheaper subsidised sugar imports pushes the four Lithuanian refineries out of the market.
Only 8,000 tonnes out of 88,000 refined in Lithuania during 1996 have been sold.

The statement also said that Lithuania was to negotiate the issue with the IMF during a planned visit of its representatives to Lithuania in mid-January. An IMF memorandum signed with Lithuania recommends the reduction of import tariffs on the basic agricultural products to 20 percent.
The average price of imported sugar is currently 2.44 litas per kilo against 2.95 for Lithuanian made sugar.
The Baltic state of Lithuania consumes 100,000-120,000 tonnes of sugar a year. --Riga newsroom + 371 721 5240
